subject: 2011 Jupiter Incident (TikTok meme)
title: What is the 2011 Jupiter Incident? A made-up TikTok space story
answer: The "2011 Jupiter Incident" is a fictional story spreading on TikTok in November 2026. Videos present it as a secret NASA crewed mission to Jupiter that went wrong, with "leaked" audio and logs. None of it happened: no astronaut has ever traveled beyond the Moon, and every mission to Jupiter has been uncrewed.
body:
The trend is a piece of internet folklore told as if it were a cover-up. A typical video plays crackly radio audio, a black screen with ominous captions or grainy space footage, and claims it is the "final transmission" from a crew that flew to Jupiter or its moon Europa in 2011. Details change from post to post: some versions say the crew found life, others say something hostile boarded the ship, and the "leak" is credited to NASA, hackers or foreign spies. Commenters play along with lines like "they never found the third astronaut" or "NASA deleted this twice."

The giveaway is in the crew list. The astronauts' names riff on the nicknames of popular streamers and meme characters, and the hashtags on many videos name those creators, so for most viewers the story is an inside joke dressed up as a creepypasta. The format borrows from analog-horror videos and "lost footage" hoaxes that have circulated online for years.

The real history is less dramatic. NASA's Juno probe did launch toward Jupiter on Aug. 5, 2011, and reached orbit on July 4, 2016, but it carries no people. Europa Clipper, launched in October 2024, is also robotic and is not due at Jupiter until 2030. The farthest humans have ever gone is the Moon, last visited by Apollo 17 in 1972; a crewed trip to Jupiter would take years each way with today's rockets.

Videos tagged with the incident multiplied in the second half of November 2026, and Google searches like "what is the Jupiter incident" began appearing on Nov. 23. For parents and teachers, it is a handy example to discuss with kids: realistic-sounding "leaks" are easy to fake, and a quick check of NASA's own mission list settles the question.
in_the_news: Short videos presenting the 2011 Jupiter Incident as a leaked NASA disaster spread on TikTok in November 2026, sending curious viewers to Google.

faq.a: No. There was no crewed mission to Jupiter in 2011 or at any other time. The only spacecraft NASA sent toward Jupiter that year was Juno, a robotic probe.

faq.q: Has anyone ever been to Jupiter?
faq.a: No person has. Only uncrewed spacecraft, such as Pioneer, Voyager, Galileo and Juno, have visited Jupiter. Humans have never traveled farther than the Moon.

faq.q: Where did the Jupiter Incident come from?
faq.a: It grew out of fictional "leaked transmission" videos on TikTok in November 2026, with crew names borrowed from streamer and meme nicknames. Creators copied the format and added their own details.

faq.q: Is the Jupiter Incident audio real NASA audio?
faq.a: No verified NASA recording matches the clips. They are edited sound effects and voices made for the meme.
